title: I Have a Dream (address at the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom)

access.edition_or_version: Delivered address, Lincoln Memorial, Washington, D.C.; transcriptions held by civil-rights archives

mechanics.premise: At the climax of the March on Washington, the speaker reframes the unmet promise of American equality as a debt still owed and a future still reachable.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Indictment of present injustice gives way to an escalating vision of resolution, ending on a note of collective freedom.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Anaphora (repeated clause-initial refrains), parallel clause series, metaphor clusters of light/dark and journey, scriptural and civic allusions; a rising cadence that functions as a peroration.
mechanics.dialogue: Direct address to the assembled marchers and to the nation; call-and-response residues of the Black folk pulpit.
mechanics.point_of_view: First-person plural 'we' fused with a prophetic first-person vision.
mechanics.tone_relevant_techniques: Model and place naming rather than abstraction; honest indictment paired with forward promise (jeremiad structure); emotional peak deferred to the close; rhythm built through repetition.
mechanics.critical_reception: Widely ranked among the most significant American speeches of the twentieth century; analysed as a fusion of prophetic preaching and civic rhetoric.
mechanics.copyright_note: Speech text remains under copyright and is not reproduced anywhere in this dossier or its records.
